title: A PS1-versus-Gaia-XP epoch survey of 29 million field dwarfs finds two multi-year dust dimmings, one new; their onset rate is below 4.4e-8 per star per year, 6 times below the prior estimate
abstract: Question: how often does slow, multi-year dust dimming start on an ordinary field dwarf? A prior estimate (2.7e-7 per star per year) rests on one event, G2870, and a 0.12-yr search window. Method: for 29.45 million Gaia DR3 dwarfs (G 14-17.65, |b| > 10 deg, Dec > -30 deg) we compared Pan-STARRS1 mean g, r, i magnitudes (2010-2014) with Gaia XP synthetic photometry (2014.6-2017.4). After a fitted colour term the residual scatter is 0.7-1.0 percent. ZTF DR24 (2018-2025) gives an independent third epoch; it agrees with the Gaia-era level of random dwarfs to 0.006 +- 0.010 mag. Results: 2,157 stars change coherently by at least 0.15 mag with dust-like colour ratios. ZTF shows that most are periodic (533), slowly varying (681) or dipping (469) stars. Of 248 changes deeper than 0.3 mag, most are photometric artefacts (scattered PS1 epochs, no Gaia scatter, ZTF equal to Gaia). Only 23 are credible: 2 are dust-like dimmers, 6 are activity cycles, 7 are periodic, 1 is bluer when fainter and 7 are unclear. The survey recovers G2870 (Delta r = -0.41 mag) and finds a new candidate, the M0 dwarf Gaia DR3 346100804155947392: quiet in 2010-2014, 0.54 mag faint (r) in the Gaia era, then aperiodic ZTF dips up to 0.94 mag with dip colour dg/dr = 1.42. Simulated trapezoid events give a 5.1-yr window for 0.5-mag, 8-yr events; the prior rate predicts 39 detections. The onset rate is 1.4e-8 per star per year (95 percent: 2.5e-9 to 4.4e-8), or below 1.1e-7 if all unclear events are dust. Limitations: the colour-ratio rule misses stochastic dippers such as G2698 because PS1 bands are not simultaneous; vetting is visual; spots and dust can have similar colours; no spectra; 0.3 percent of the area failed. display.caption: Onset rate of multi-year deep dimming events per star per year. Lines: 95 percent upper limits from this survey for event depths 0.5, 1 and 2 mag against event duration (solid: 2 vetted dust events; dashed: if all 7 unclear deep events were dust). Square: measured rate for 0.5-mag, 8-yr events with 95 percent interval. Band and line: the prior G2870-like estimate (sci:sha256:db7ac295) with its 68 percent interval.

Three-epoch light curves on the PS1 system: PS1 epochs (2010-2014, large dots), the Gaia-era XP synthetic level (bars, 2014.6-2017.4) and ZTF nights (2018-2025). Top: the recovered one-off dimmer G2870 and the new dust-like candidate Gaia DR3 346100804155947392. Middle and bottom: the contaminant classes (activity cycle, eclipsing binary, bluer-when-fainter variable, PS1 artefact).

a: fraction of 29.45 million dwarfs with a coherent g, r, i change larger than |Delta r| between PS1 and Gaia XP, for fades and rises, all and credible. b: ZTF third-epoch classes of the 2,157 candidates by direction and depth. c: detection window at |Delta r| >= 0.3 mag for trapezoid events of depth 0.5, 1 and 2 mag, compared with the 0.12-yr window of the prior search.
